## RYANAIR DELIVERS RECORD PORTO WINTER 2026 SCHEDULE WITH TWO ADDITIONAL BASED AIRCRAFT


### 14 AIRCRAFT ($1.4BN INVESTMENT), 55 ROUTES (7 NEW), AND 2.7M WINTER SEATS (+13%)


Ryanair, Europe’s No.1 airline, today (Tues, 3 Nov) announced its record Winter 2026 schedule for Porto, delivering 2.7m Winter seats (+13%) across 55 routes, including 7 exciting new routes to Catania, Gdansk, Hamburg, Liverpool, Nuremberg, Poznan, and Rabat, offering Portuguese citizens/visitors in the Norte Region even more choice at the lowest fares in Europe.


This substantial growth is supported by Ryanair’s addition of 2 new based aircraft at Porto for Winter 2026, representing an incremental $200m investment. Ryanair’s expanded Porto operation will continue to drive year-round traffic and tourism while supporting over 5,300 local jobs across the Norte Region.


**Ryanair’s Porto Winter 2026 schedule will deliver:**


- 55 routes, incl. 7 new routes to Catania, Gdansk, Hamburg, Liverpool, Nuremberg, Poznan, and Rabat
- 2 new based aircraft (14 total) – $1.4bn investment
- Increased freq. on 28 existing routes
- 2.7m seats, incl. +315,000 additional seats (+13%)
- 6.2m passengers p.a. (+4%)
- Supp. over 5,300 local jobs, incl. 420 highly‑paid local pilot and cabin crew jobs


To celebrate Ryanair’s record Porto Winter 2026 schedule the airline has launched a limited-time seat sale with fares from just €29.99 available to book now via the Ryanair App/website.


**Ryanair CEO, Eddie Wilson, said:**


*“As Europe’s No.1 airline, Ryanair is delighted to announce its record schedule and 2 new based aircraft in Porto for Winter 2026, representing an additional $200m investment in the Norte Region. These 2 new aircraft bring Ryanair’s Porto-based fleet to 14 aircraft ($1.4bn investment) and will deliver an additional 315,000 low-fare Ryanair seats (+13%) this Winter across 55 routes, including 7 new routes to Catania, Gdansk, Hamburg, Liverpool, Nuremberg, Poznan, and Rabat. Ryanair’s expanded Porto operation will continue to drive year-round traffic and tourism while supporting over 5,300 local jobs, including 420 highly‑paid local pilot and cabin crew jobs, across the Norte Region.”*
